declarations.description:
A line chart over a time or numeric x axis, drawn on canvas by uPlot.

Series are declared as `c2-chart-series` children — the same authoring shape as `c2-table`'s columns —
or through the `series` property. With neither, one line is drawn per numeric key of the first row.

```html
<c2-line-chart x-type="time" x-field="t" legend="bottom" data='[{ "t": 1704067200000, "cpu": 12 }]'>
  <c2-chart-series field="cpu" label="CPU"></c2-chart-series>
</c2-line-chart>
```

Realtime feeds should call `appendPoint()` rather than reassigning `data`: it writes into the frame's
spare capacity and redraws without a Lit update.

declarations.description:

extends `c2-line-chart` and every one of its attributes (`curve`, `points`, `zoom`, the axis bounds)
means the same thing here.

```html
<c2-area-chart x-type="time" x-field="t" fill-opacity="0.2" data="[]">
  <c2-chart-series field="sessions" label="Sessions"></c2-chart-series>
</c2-area-chart>
```

members.name: decorateOptions
members.description:
Strips every remaining pixel of chrome, so the line fills the whole box.

The axes are left alone on purpose: `this.axes = 'none'` already builds them with `show: false`, which
is what makes uPlot skip both the axis element and its gutter. Handing it `axes: []` would do the
opposite — uPlot fills a short array back up to two axes with its own defaults, which are *visible* —
and a 120x32 sparkline would spend 52px of its width on a y axis it never asked for.

declarations.description:
Shared behaviour of every `c2-*-chart`: the chrome and its slots, the resize observer, theme
resolution, data normalisation, and the routing that keeps a realtime update off the expensive path.
It defines no tag and is never registered — the concrete charts extend it.

**Why the data and presentation inputs are separate.** `data` and `revision` are the only properties on
the data path; everything else is presentation. A change limited to the data path is pushed straight
into the engine from `shouldUpdate`, which returns `false`, so Lit never renders or commits and the
canvas container is not touched. Anything else rebuilds the engine options, which is allowed to be
expensive. That is what makes a streaming tick cost one engine redraw and nothing more.

**Sizing.** A canvas has no intrinsic size, so the host is sized by `--c2-chart--height` (320px by
default) rather than by its content. Give the host a height — through the variable, a CSS rule, or a
flex parent — or the plot area collapses.

element already has, and shadowing it breaks the Web Animations API on the host.

events.name: tooltip-change
events.description: Fired with the complete tooltip model as the pointer moves, and with `null` when it leaves. Used by `c2-chart-tooltip`.

events.name: series-toggle
events.description: Fired when a legend entry is toggled. Does not bubble.

events.name: legend-change
events.description: Fired when legend entries or visibility change. Used by `c2-chart-legend`.

events.name: range-change
events.description: Fired after the user zooms or brushes. `detail.min` and `detail.max` are the new x bounds. Does not bubble.

events.name: chart-ready
events.description: Fired after the engine has loaded and drawn for the first time. The host also gains `data-chart-ready`, which is what a test should wait on.

events.name: chart-error
events.description: Fired when the engine fails to load or to draw. `detail.error` is the underlying failure.

events.name: point-hover
events.description: Fired as the pointer moves between data points, and with a `null` detail when it leaves the plot. Does not bubble.

events.name: point-click
events.description: Fired when a datum is clicked. Does not bubble: several components fire point events, so a listener belongs on the element itself.
